title: Perfect complexes are the saturated triangulated closure of the ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. In the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the full subcategory of perfect objects [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] is the smallest strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory containing the unit object $A[0]$. Here strictly full means closed under isomorphism, and saturated means closed under direct summands. Equivalently, this is the thick subcategory generated by $A[0]$ [pur9-def-thick]: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts, distinguished cones and direct summands.

source.place: Tag 0ATI, lemma-perfect-ring-classical-generator; terminology in derived.tex, definition-saturated (Tag 05RB) and definition-triangulated-subcategory

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the full subcategory of $D(A)$ consisting of perfect objects. If $C_1\to C_2\to C_3\to C_1[1]$ is a distinguished triangle and $C_1,C_3$ are perfect, then $C_2$ is perfect by [lem-sf-perfect-ring-triangle-closure].

source.place: Tag 0ATI, proof, paragraph beginning `It was shown in Lemmas` (using Tag 066R)

proof.text: The other two two-out-of-three cases follow by rotating the distinguished triangle and using closure under integer shifts (Step 3): if $C_2,C_3$ are perfect, the backward rotation $C_3[-1]\to C_1\to C_2\to C_3$ is distinguished and has perfect first and third terms $C_3[-1],C_2$, so $C_1$ is perfect by [lem-sf-perfect-ring-triangle-closure]; if $C_1,C_2$ are perfect, the rotation $C_2\to C_3\to C_1[1]\to C_2[1]$ has perfect first and third terms, so $C_3$ is perfect. The rotations in both directions are axiom (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Thus $\mathcal P$ is triangulated.

source.place: Tag 0ATI, proof, paragraph beginning `It was shown in Lemmas`

proof.text: The zero complex is bounded with finitely generated projective terms, and an isomorphism of perfect objects remains perfect after composing its representing isomorphism. Shifting a bounded finite-projective complex reindexes its finite-projective terms, and a finite direct sum of two such complexes is again bounded with finitely generated projective terms. Hence $\mathcal P$ is strictly full, contains zero, and is closed under shifts and finite direct sums.

source.place: Tag 0ATI, proof, paragraph beginning `It was shown in Lemmas`

proof.text: If K is a retract of a perfect object L, complete its split inclusion to a distinguished triangle K → L → Z → K[1]. The first map is monic, so the connecting map is zero and the split-triangle isomorphism identifies L with K ⊕ Z. Apply [lem-sf-perfect-ring-summand] to conclude that K is perfect. Together with Steps 1–3, this makes the perfect object property thick.

source.place: Tag 0ATI, proof, paragraph beginning `It was shown in Lemmas` (using Tag 066S)

proof.text: The unit $A[0]$ is represented by the one-term complex with the finitely generated free (hence projective) module $A$ in degree zero, so $A[0]\in\mathcal P$ by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

source.place: Tag 0ATI, proof, sentence `Of course R \in D_{perf}(R)`

proof.text: Let T be a thick object property containing A[0]. It is closed under binary and finite products by the distinguished split triangle [lem-sbc-biproduct-triangle-distinguished] and the zero object. For a finite projective module M, choose a finite free surjection A^n → M; projectivity splits it. Apply singleFunctor in degree zero to this actual retract. Its ambient finite free object is the image of the finite product of A, hence lies in T. Retract closure gives M[0] in T, and the single-functor shift isomorphism gives M in every degree. This argument includes n=0 and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 0ATI, proof, induction base `By definition \langle R \rangle_1 contains any finite projective R-module`

proof.text: Use the equivalent induction peeling off the lowest term, with the existing proved stupid-truncation construction [lem-sf-module-stupid-truncation-short-exact] from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.ModuleCatTelescope. For a bounded finite-projective model L in [a,b], let S_c = σ^{≥c}L. The object Q(S_{b+1}) is zero. Induct on n to show Q(S_{b+1-n}) lies in T. The short exact sequence 0 → S_{c+1} → S_c → L^c[-c] → 0 gives the distinguished triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The first term belongs to T by induction and the third by Step 6, so the middle does too. At n=(b+1-a).toNat the truncation is isomorphic to L, since its cutoff is at most a. This also treats empty intervals. Finally transport membership along the representing isomorphism of [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

proof.text: By [pur9-def-thick], the thick subcategory generated by $A[0]$ is the intersection of all thick subcategories containing it. Steps 1--4 show that the perfect subcategory is one such thick subcategory, while the induction shows that every such subcategory contains every perfect object. Therefore the intersection equals $\mathcal P$, proving that the perfect objects are the smallest strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory containing $A[0]$.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Tag 0ATI and its induction proof. The perfect subcategory is shown triangulated using the existing ring triangle-closure lemma and triangulated rotations, strictly full and closed under shifts and finite sums directly from the definition, and saturated using the new ring-level direct-summand statement from Tag 066S. The reverse inclusion is the source's induction on the length of a bounded finite-projective representative, using the stupid truncation triangle; the intersection characterization is the thick-subcategory definition.
